annotations.text:
What these replace

Every project without a screenshot currently renders the same CSS browser-window placeholder — a title bar, a sidebar, three grey rows. Eight exhibits, one identical picture, and a fake browser says nothing true about a C tool that reads /proc.

These are drawn per project instead.

Where each drawing comes from

02 schedule blocks — event platform
03 graph resolving into a ranked list — Cypher over 5,000+ records, custom ranking
04 five API pills into one dossier — the aggregation you describe
05 phone feed plus check marks — announcements, JUnit/Mockito
06 three loose plans into one date — planning and coordination
07 nearly empty — a daily reminder to enjoy life
08 /proc meters plus fork and pipes — signals, concurrency

Nothing is claimed that the descriptions don't already say.

These are covers, not screenshots. A real screenshot beats a drawing every time for anything live — Personal Website and the Analysis Tool both have repos, so if you can grab captures I'd use those and keep the drawings for the ones with nothing to show.

Hack the Valley is still the thin one: its description is a single sentence, so its cover is the most generic of the eight.
